title: How to Add Details Without Memorising
answer_framework:
Examiners can easily spot memorised answers. Instead of memorising scripts, you should learn to dynamically add details using the 'Sensory & Opinion' expansion.

Whenever you mention a noun, attach a detail to it:
1. Sensory Details: What did it look, sound, smell, or taste like? (e.g., Instead of 'We ate cake', say 'We ate a rich, dark chocolate cake that was incredibly moist').
2. Opinion Details: Attach your personal feeling to the event. (e.g., Instead of 'The train was late', say 'The train was delayed, which was incredibly frustrating because I was rushing').

This method ensures your answer is always unique, detailed, and completely natural.
useful_phrase_bank: It had this incredibly ... vibe to it. (Sensory)
What I vividly remember is the smell/sound of ... (Sensory)
I was completely blown away by ... (Opinion)

weak_vs_better.weak_answer: The hotel room was big and nice. I liked it.
weak_vs_better.better_answer: The hotel room was remarkably spacious, with these huge floor-to-ceiling windows that let in so much natural light. I was completely blown away by the stunning view of the city skyline.

fluency_pronunciation_note: When adding adjectives (like 'remarkably spacious' or 'stunning view'), put a slight emphasis (word stress) on the adjective. This demonstrates control over sentence stress and makes you sound much more engaging.
sample_ielts_question: Describe a place you visited on holiday.
model_short_answer: I visited a small coastal village in Italy. Instead of just saying 'it was beautiful', I'd add details: The village was perched on a steep cliff, and the air always had this crisp, salty smell to it. I was absolutely mesmerised by the pastel-coloured houses.
common_mistakes: Using generic adjectives like 'good', 'nice', 'bad', 'big' instead of descriptive ones.
Sounding robotic because the details were pre-memorised rather than naturally thought of in the moment.
image_prompt_fallback: A breathtaking view of a tropical beach with clear blue water and vibrant green palm trees, emphasizing sensory visual details.

quiz.question: Which of the following is an example of a 'Sensory Detail'?

options.A: I think it is a very important issue.
options.B: The coffee shop had a rich aroma of freshly roasted beans.
options.C: I went there with my brother last Tuesday.
options.D: It is located in the center of the city.

quiz.explanation: Option B describes a smell ('rich aroma'), engaging the senses. This type of description naturally boosts vocabulary and makes the answer more vivid.
